Set up a runtime L133: L134: Runtime components read their state from an assistant-ui runtime. Add one to an existing project: L135: L136: `npx assistant-ui@latest init` L137: Then wrap your app in a runtime provider: L138: L139: `import { AssistantRuntimeProvider } from "@assistant-ui/react"; L140: import { useChatRuntime, AssistantChatTransport } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk"; L141: L142: export default function App() { L143: const runtime = useChatRuntime({ L144: transport: new AssistantChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat" }), L145: }); L146: L147: return ( L148: L149: {/* your components */} L150: L151: ); L152: }` L153: The 【176†installation guide】 covers new projects, templates, and API routes. L154: L155: This component is composed from runtime primitives and has no standalone build. L156: L157: File renders one file message part. Playable `audio/*` and `video/*` files stay inline with their player, filename, optional size, and download link. Every other file remains the compact icon row. With a runtime it renders straight from a message's file part; standalone you hand it the part yourself. ` L207: L208: The player shows the filename as its title. L209: The icon row remains for non-media files. `File.Player` routes playable audio and video data to the matching player: `http(s)`, `blob:`, and `data:` URLs are safe to play, and raw base64 becomes a data URI with the part's MIME type. An `id` or another URL scheme keeps the plain row. The icon depends on `mimeType`: images get an image icon, PDFs and other text get a document icon, JSON gets a braces icon, audio and video get their own icons, and everything else gets a generic file icon. L210: `sourceType` states how `data` is encoded on the wire: `"url"` for a link, `"id"` for an opaque reference the download link can't resolve on its own, or omitted to infer it. The size row only appears for inline data (base64 or a `data:` URI), since a URL or id reference carries no byte count to read. Pass to `MessagePrimitive.Parts` as `components.File`. L266: `File.Root` | `div` | Row with `variant` and `size`. L267: `File.Icon` | `span` | Icon chosen from `mimeType`. L268: `File.Name` | `span` | Filename text; shows "Unnamed file" when empty. `File`'s own row passes it the `mimeType` label instead. L269: `File.Size` | `span` | Formatted byte size; you supply `bytes`. L270: `File.Download` | `a` | Download link; `null` when `data` can't produce a safe `href`. L271: `File.Player` | `div` | Routes playable audio and video files to the matching inline player; `null` otherwise. L272: ### 【186†File part】 L273: Field | Type | Description L274: --- | --- | --- L275: `filename` | `string` | Optional display name; without one, the icon row of a non-media file shows a label derived from `mimeType`, such as "PDF file". L276: `data` | `string` | The file payload: base64, a `data:` URI, or a URL/id per `sourceType`. L277: `mimeType` | `string` | Drives the icon and, for base64/`data:` payloads, the download `href`. L278: `sourceType` | `"url" | "id"` | Optional. States how to interpret `data`; omitted infers from its shape.
